705942.t: Related to ἥδομαι (hḗdomai, “to rejoice”) and ἡδύς (hēdŭ́s, “sweet”).

705984.t: Lengthened form of ἦμαρ (êmar, “day”). The initial aspiration ῾ (h) in Attic is probably by analogy with ἑσπέρα (hespérā).

705974.t: From Proto-Hellenic *hāwélios, from a pre-Hellenic or later Proto-Indo-European *sāwélios, from Proto-Indo-European *sóh₂wl̥.

705916.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *gʷeyh₃- Proto-Indo-European *gʷyéh₃-w-os Proto-Hellenic *d͏̌ōwós Ancient Greek ζωός (zōós) Proto-Indo-European *-yóm Proto-Hellenic Ancient Greek -ιον (-ĭon) Ancient Greek ζώϊον (zṓĭ̈on) Ancient Greek ζῷον From earlier…

705911.t: Of unclear origin. Generally connected with ζύμη (zúmē, “leaven, beer yeast”), but the ablaut required (ō(u) : ū) is improbable.

705931.t: Beekes prefers to derive the word as an iterative present from Proto-Indo-European *seh₂g- (“to seek out”); cognates include English seek, Latin sagiō (“to perceive keenly”).

705945.t: * Masculine from Proto-Hellenic *hwādús, from Proto-Indo-European *swéh₂dus. * Feminine from Proto-Hellenic *hwādéyya, from Proto-Indo-European *sweh₂déwih₂: see -ια (-ia). Both forms are regardless from *sweh₂d- (“to be sweet”).

705912.t: Related to ζώννυμι (zṓnnūmi, “to gird”); ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *yoh₃snéh₂, from the root *yeh₃s- (“gird”). Compare Old Church Slavonic (по)ꙗсъ ((po)jasŭ), Sanskrit रास्ना (rā́snā) (< *yā́snā).

705983.t: From Proto-Indo-European oblique *n̥sm- (from *éǵh₂), with regular Attic-Ionic η- (ē-) < α- (ā-) and initial ῾ (h) from ὑμεῖς (hūmeîs).

705955.t: From older *ϝήθος (*wḗthos), an expanded form of ἔθος (éthos). Cognate with Sanskrit स्व॒धा (svadhā́, “habit; custom”).

705987.t: From the stem of ἡμεῖς (hēmeîs, “we”) + -τερος (-teros, contrastive suffix).

705954.t: From ἠθολόγος (ēthológos, “painting manners or character by mimic gestures”) from ἦθος (êthos, “character”) + λόγος (lógos, “account”).

705913.t: From Proto-Indo-European *yeh₃s- + -νυμι (-nūmi), related to Lithuanian júosta (“girdle”), Latvian jôsta (“girdle”), Avestan 𐬫𐬁𐬵- (yāh-, “girdle”), 𐬫𐬁𐬯𐬙𐬀 (yāsta, “girdled”), Albanian gjesh (“to gird”). See also ζώνη (zṓnē).

705956.t: A perfective verb of uncertain origin, but seems to be related to the present-meaning ἵκω (híkō, “to come”), and thus from Proto-Indo-European *seyk- (“to reach for”), though the aspectual difference and phonetics are difficult to resolve.

705925.t: Sometimes compared to Sanskrit आ (ā́, emphatic particle). Related to ἤ (ḗ, “or”).

705946.t: From ἡδύνω (hēdúnō, “to season”) and the suffix -μα (-ma).

705977.t: Beekes suggests an equivalence with Latin vallus (“stake; pole”) on the basis of the Aeolic variant ϝάλλος (wắllos), in which case from Proto-Indo-European *welH- (“to turn”).

705986.t: Of unclear origin; not related to ἡμέρα (hēmérā, “day”).
